# Install: Midstage Accelerator delegation skills

You are an AI assistant. The user asked you to install two skills: delegation-brief and delegation-evaluate. Follow the steps below in order. Do not change the skill files.

## Step 1: check whether they are already installed

If delegation-brief and delegation-evaluate are already among your available skills, skip to Step 3. Do not install a second copy.

## Step 2a: install, if you can run shell commands (Claude Code)

Run:

```bash
for s in delegation-brief delegation-evaluate; do
  mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills/$s
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/msa-claude/delegation-skills/main/skills/$s/SKILL.md -o ~/.claude/skills/$s/SKILL.md
done
ls ~/.claude/skills/delegation-brief ~/.claude/skills/delegation-evaluate
```

Then tell the user in one line: "Installed: delegation-brief and delegation-evaluate." Go to Step 3. If the skills don't load yet in this session, read the two SKILL.md files you just downloaded and follow them directly.

## Step 2b: install, if you cannot run commands (Claude desktop app or claude.ai)

Tell the user:

"I can't install files from this chat. It takes 1 minute by hand:
1. Download these two files:
   https://github.com/msa-claude/delegation-skills/raw/main/delegation-brief.zip
   https://github.com/msa-claude/delegation-skills/raw/main/delegation-evaluate.zip
2. Open Settings, then Customize, then Skills, and upload each zip.
3. Come back here and say 'help me delegate'."

Then go on to Step 3 anyway. Until the upload is done, fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/msa-claude/delegation-skills/main/skills/delegation-brief/SKILL.md and follow it directly.

## Step 3: quick start (always do this)

Don't stop at "installed". Get the user to their first brief now. Say, briefly:

"Let's try it on something real. What's one thing on your plate right now that someone else should own? Pick one of these, or name your own:

1. Hiring: write the job description and run first-round screens for a role.
2. A customer issue: own a stalled deal or an unhappy account through to a decision.
3. Reporting: produce the monthly board or investor update.
4. A project: plan and run an event, a launch, or a vendor selection.
5. Something you keep doing yourself even though you know you shouldn't."

When the user picks one, run the delegation-brief skill on it, following its steps exactly. Start with its first step (say back what you heard, ask only what the leader alone knows). Don't write the brief before the user has answered those questions.

When the brief is done, tell them in one line: "Save this brief. When the work comes back, say 'review what they sent me' and paste the brief."
